question: On KODEX 200 with the same lump sum, window, valuation clock, integer shares and ETF costs, how do the EMA ribbon (operating paper rule), AdxSmas and mabStra (rung-2 freqtrade results, replayed) and buy-and-hold compare in return and drawdown?

windows.A: 2022-11-23..2025-12-30 (a past window not used by the 52-strategy sweep; KODEX daily history was seen in the ribbon research, so not called unseen)

capital: 10,000,000 won at the first session of the window, no deposits, no withdrawals
prices: raw (unadjusted) prices from the fixed KODEX 1m snapshot user_data/data_kodex/source_snapshot/069500.csv (ee10cfe3): session open = open of the first minute bar, session close = close of the last minute bar (closing-auction print); dividends are ignored for every method alike
valuation: equity = cash + shares x session close, every session of the window, for every method; max drawdown is computed on this daily equity series for all methods
costs: 0.015% commission on each side (ETF, no sell tax), integer shares; no extra slippage for any method (the freqtrade fills are at bar opens without slippage, so the rule-based methods get the same treatment); a +-5 won per share slippage sensitivity is reported separately

methods.hold: buy the affordable integer shares at the first session open, hold to the last session close
methods.ribbon: EMA 8>21>50>200 on adjusted daily closes from the 2002-10-14 origin (kodex_daily_adj.json, the operating rule core definition); decision at each session close; execution at the next session open, all-in or all-out with integer shares; the position on the first session is decided by the close before the window
methods.AdxSmas_replay: trades from results/rung2_v1/<window>/AdxSmas replayed on the same valuation clock: cash changes by amount x rate x (1 +- fee) at each fill; parity check: final equity must equal the engine's final balance x 10,000

no_claim: one instrument, two windows; descriptive comparison only, not a profitability proof or a live approval
